An abandoned module persists in `loose[]` as left and the derelict persists as left (WM-24, WM-28, IA-28); dropped in the dark it cannot be re-taken until something lights it (IA-28). **There is no forced drop, no hop refusal with cargo, and no tool kills a horror**: nothing is a weapon (anti-pillar), and the MVP kit has no repel tool (`tool_suppressant` is removed, user ruling X6 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the HE-39 repel stays a dormant [CUT-FIRST] interface). A horror met during a carry is answered by retreat, stillness, darkness or 'drop the cargo', which the user confirmed as the intended price of hauling (D63: Horror's figures have a carrier who keeps the cargo struck on 7 of 18 draws, with `R_SNAP_PX` 48 the lever); Horror places nothing in salvage and has no edge to author (HE:376, Designed). Every sortie step from the cut to the hop (steps 8 to 12) therefore has a legal exit. *Why.* A carried module that cannot be abandoned would turn a tell into a sentence. *Pillar.* P2, P3; anti-pillar (not a combat game). *Decided.* run rulings R13, R25. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Gating note (ruled; numbers pending).** The conditions are legal as written, and the decision they serve (keep walking, or set it down) is made live by the ruling of OQ-BS-27 (option B: the carry-state intake plus the lengthened carry, D.2 and D.3). It is live in kind (the tell opens inside the carry, holding cargo never outwaits it, and a drop does) and thin in margin: Attention's recalibration is run (F-26) and leaves a live share of 140 permille of the tell draw at 28 tiles, none at 21 to 24, and 66 to 140 permille over the lit pre-lift dwell sweep (D.2, D.3); the pass line is the boarding spike's (AC-BS-132, delegated ruling R5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. **The stake of walking on** (named so that the choice is read and not learned as a clock) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a walker whose drawn tell is shorter than the carry ahead arrives after `breach_due_T` and takes the breach (STRESS on the locus body, the beacon, the web's attention at the rim), a walker who arrives first voids it at no cost (AT-22), and the draw is never shown (P1); at the placeholders walking on wins in about 86 percent of draws at the reference carry, which Attention measures (AC-AT-134); OQ-AT-36 is decided (leave it, measured; delegated ruling R21, 2026-10-28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Precondition (answered)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21; G1, the publisher's answer stands and Boarding conforms)*: a horror may path or stand in `a_spine` at the MVP (Horror E-HE-59, HE-26 and Horror's Dependencies row for Boarding & Salvage; ASK-BS-H1, OQ-BS-33 answered). No bypass and no wider spine is required or asked: the spine is the 3-wide corridor with no side step (DA-48, 3 x 23) and the legal-exit claim stands, because every step from the cut to the hop (steps 8 to 12) still has a legal exit and the exit is priced, not free. A carrier who meets a horror in the spine has the ruled answers and no new one: drop the cargo (BS-13 d) and walk back the way it came, which may be toward the cold `a_machine` (a priced exit, not a sentence); stand still and go dark if no other light reaches the seat (HE-13); or shut a door behind it (V4 `set_opening` on a door face is carry-admitted, BS-9, and a closed leaf is solid to the horror, HE-26). A carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws with `R_SNAP_PX` 48 the lever (D63, confirmed as the price of hauling). The pressure of being met in the one corridor of the carry is the dread Pillars 2 and 3 aim for. A spine end that is a dead end failing Horror's `DEAD_END_NARROW` lint is Derelict Authoring's defect (E-HE-26), not a Boarding rule. No story is opened for BS-13's decision-bearing rows or for the tell acceptance rows that need a sortie-produced tell (AC-BS-72, AC-BS-122, AC-BS-123, the crossing clause of AC-BS-14b) until AC-BS-123 passes on the regenerated `REF_GOLDEN`. The fixture-armed mechanics rows (AC-BS-17, 18, 34, 35, 87, 93) test Attention's and Web Map's owned behaviour with `attention_arm_tell` and stay open as contract tests.

**BS-14 — Field checks: the procedure and the ladder (class (d) hooks).** *Rule.* Interaction owns the `field_check` channel (IA-30); Sanity owns lure data, `lures[]`, the ledger and `record_falsification(player_id, check_kind, subject_ref, outcome)` (SN-17, Class B); the Item DB owns true mass and the junk defs (IDB-22, VS-A). **Boarding owns the procedure**: when a crew runs the ladder during a sortie, its preconditions, and what each rung costs in the sortie's budget. The ladder is SN-21's, cheapest first:

| Rung | Instrument | Cost inside the sortie | Tier | Precondition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The **weight breath-step**: pick it up and feel `cue_load` (SE-28) | the pickup, then `drop` if suspect; no tool, no channel | MVP on real modules and the hull plate; lures VS-A | the stowed class is below the carried class under test (`STOWED_CUE_FLOOR_CLASS` [PLACEHOLDER]): **drop the plate first** |
| 2 | **SCAN** (`check_kind` SCAN) | `FIELD_CHECK_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER], lit, scanner in hand (slot 3), plus the swap | MVP (the scanner is an honest anchor, SN-19) | scanner held; hands free |
| 3 | **PALETTE** (the violet or flesh leak on the sprite) | sight only | VS-A | the Perception Filter (Designed) |
| 4 | The **authored-absence read**: undisturbed dust, a missing verdict trail, a dried trail on a module's own fitting (DA:1189; FT:71 "a candidate field check, never a guarantee") | walking and looking | MVP | exists only where Derelict Authoring placed a dead fault |
| 5 | **The trip home** | the dearest | MVP | none |

A rung can fail to *apply* (a stowed HEAVY, no scanner, no authored trail) but never lies in the MVP; no result is stored as truth about a lie in `interaction.state` (IA-30). The design test is Sanity's `C_check <= 0.05 x T_home` (SN-21 and the class (d) design test of SN D.7, where `T_home` is "the one-way trip home with the item"), and the break-even walk-versus-scan distance `d*` is 5 tiles (SN-18, AC-SN-70); whether SCAN passes the test on the MVP routes is a finding in Formulas (`check_cost_ratio`), not a rule. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **SCAN is an explicit MVP exception to SN-21 and SN D.7's 5 percent test**: it passes on no MVP route (0.250 to 0.056), class (d) ships no junk for it to disprove, and the exception lapses at VS-A, where either the junk placement keeps `T_home` at least 3120 ticks (D.7) or `FIELD_CHECK_TICKS` is bounded at 66 or less (`C_check` = 36 + 66 = 102 and `20 * 102` = 2040 is at most the 2055 ticks of reading (c) for `htr_a`; it still fails readings (a) and (b)). IA-30 reserves `check_kind` HEFT (the lift-and-weigh) and PALETTE for VS-A; at MVP rung 1 is perception only (SE-28) and records nothing, and the recorded form is HEFT at VS-A. **"Drop the plate first" is not yet performable**: the plate is a STOWED stack, `drop` (IA-28) releases only the carried instance, and no in-world way to shed a stowed stack is written (ASK-BS-S1); until one is, the ladder skips rung 1 and uses SCAN or the trip home. MVP exercises: the breath-step on real carried modules and the plate, SCAN, and the absence read on `scr_a` (BS-17). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **No scanner additions at the MVP** (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D66): no scanner cooldown, no within-band magnitude-only GLIDE and no rebuild of Sanity's D.12; Sanity's rung-mix telemetry (AC-SN-165) decides later. Class (d) itself is VS-A; its acceptance rows are **deferred**, blockers "junk defs (IDB-22) + the Perception Filter + SN-21", and the blind two-clip audio identification test of the load cue (SE RK-2, at least 90 %) is a precondition of the VS-A breath-step. *Why.* The trip home is the fallback, not the only reveal (Pillar 4(d)). *Pillar.* P4. *Decided.* run ruling R17.

**BS-15 — The lie is in the prize, never in the price.** *Rule.* A hallucination may lie about **what** a module is or **whether** it is worth taking. It may never lie about **what taking it costs**: the cut's noise, the stub's hiss, the load's breath, the carry's pace, the time, the air. Each price channel is truthful by its owner's rule: noise is Attention's (IA-33, ART 2.7), hiss and room air are on the Graph's closed consequence list (LSG:44), the breath comes from true `mass_g` (SE-28, IDB-22), the pace is `V_CARRY` (PC-8), the beam is the truth anchor (EM). The carry burden is a price as well, and in the fiction it is keyed on place: **the web hears the taking at the wreck**, so the burden runs while salvage is held aboard the locus it was taken from and stops at the pod (EC-BS-63); no hallucination changes it (Attention owns it, F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. A phantom has no subject and answers like an unlit object (EM-21, IA-13), so reaching for one is not a free oracle. The MVP ships class (b) only. *Why.* If the price could lie the bargain is meaningless and the player stops making it; if only the prize can lie, every take is a bet on one's own perception and the ladder is how it is bought down. *Pillar.* P4, P1. *Decided.* creative-director guard rail G-11.

**BS-16 — The faucet is finite and persists as left.** *Rule.* Salvage is the only faucet (IDB-29): the authored module-node list (A 18 module nodes, B 22, home 26, DA-21), the seeded loose ledger (9 placements, DA-26) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and `salvage_yield` (deterministic, no RNG, salvage-once, IDB-17). A SALVAGED slot is a tombstone and stays so (LSG:243). A left derelict stands exactly as left (WM-24, WM-28). The remaining salvage in a room is read from the room (the empty pedestal rect, LY-20; the scorched kerf; hissing or capped stubs; an empty shelf), never from a count (ART 7.4). Repeated as Derelict Authoring asks (DA:1239): **the faucet is the authored node list and loose placements; the ledger is finite; and a cheap field read exists for a failed module** (BS-14, BS-17). Sortie-level loose-item rules only: an abandoned item persists (BS-13); a yield appears at the node anchor; items are section-local, so a weld or detach moves nothing (LY-22). Compartment-level "first entry" knowledge is **not** Boarding's and is declined at MVP: Web Map keeps the derelict level (`FIRST_BOARDED`, WM-28), Layout keeps only `room_at`, and the owner is the Vertical Slice Knowledge Codex's PROFILE-scoped data (answering LY Open Question 12). *Why.* A faucet the player can read from the room and cannot refill is what makes scarcity push inward; a count, a first-entry flag or any regrowth would each be a meter or a farm. *Pillar.* P5 (a finite persisting list vs a refillable crate, finite). *Decided.* run rulings R11, R20.

**BS-17 — The taught payoff of sortie A is `htr_a`; `scr_a` is optional restraint.** *Rule.* The **reference first sortie** cuts `htr_a` (MEDIUM 12000 g, power-only so no stub, in `a_machine`) and installs it in the vacant `hp_cargo_heater`, which arms PWR-OVL at home (MSA:28, DA-12, DA:855): a consequence the player caused. **`a_machine` is the one lethal-cold room**, so the reference sortie is a *hazard* sortie: the carried round trip through an unbreathable stretch and the hazard crossing are bounded by Derelict Authoring's lints (BS-20) and the room's tell is the frost creeping over the sill of the closed door before it is opened. The dead scrubber `scr_a` (FAILED, `hp` 2000, HEAVY 40000 g, `a_life`) is a legal cut whose carry home **now has a destination** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (user ruling D72: a vacant scrubber hardpoint at home, with two or three competing hardpoints, which are Assembly's data and Derelict Authoring's placement; there is still no `remove_module`, MSA-28), so installing it installs a FAILED module with no take-back (BS-18) and the beat is a stake and not only "the time the loot was garbage" (concept Key Dynamics); it remains Derelict Authoring's *quiet alternative* (cut it and leave; DA:1157). This GDD does **not** script `scr_a` as the first or the reference cut (IDB-14): the first cut is `htr_a`, and reading `scr_a` is what its destination is for. *Falsifier of record for `scr_a` before the cut* (DA OQ-V10): **only what is on the Graph's closed consequence list** — lamp brightness (its NODE_LANTERN dark, the lamp-free neighbour branch, DA-24, DA:1445), the room's own O2 and temperature as the body feels them, draught — plus **SCAN as the priced second instrument**. The cut's missing hum is true-state audio in the consequence channel (LSG:976) but is not in LSG:44's enumerated list; Boarding uses it as true-state corroboration and does not make it the falsifier of record until the Graph rules (C-BS-4). On A's dead bus nothing hums, so the hum, like the lantern, falsifies 'running' only; the dead-bus analysis is unchanged; undisturbed dust is supporting verdict grammar (ART 6.5). **Weight cannot discriminate**: `scr_a` has the same def mass, 40000 g, as a healthy scrubber. **On a dead bus the closed-list witnesses falsify "running" only**: on A's dead bus no machine runs, so every lantern is dark, `scr_a`'s and `pump_a`'s alike (DA-24), and the room's O2 and temperature cannot tell an unpowered healthy scrubber from a FAILED one; health is discriminated by SCAN, or by waking the bus with the spare breaker (DA-25, AC-DA-111), after which `pump_a`'s lantern lights and `scr_a`'s stays dark. *Conditions (creative-director D-CD-3):* the beat is honest only if the falsifier works in playtest (playtest target X-BS-3, Game Feel and AC-BS-71); if it does not, the beat is a trap and the response is routed to the falsifier (the witnesses of record, the SCAN cost), because the content route is already committed (user ruling D72) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Conflicts routed: C-BS-3 (LS-26 "first V8" names `scr_a`), C-BS-4, C-BS-6 (DA playtest target X-DA-8). *Pillar.* P1 (no payoff-less carry is taught), P4, P5. *Decided.* run rulings R10, R18; creative-director D-CD-3.

**BS-18 — Install at home: the precondition repeated.** *Rule.* `install_module {hardpoint_ref}` is Assembly's PLAYER TAP and its prompt exists iff the seat carries an instance whose def is in `compatible_defs(h)` for the focused HARDPOINT (immediate, never an oracle); the chain is M5 `install_module`, `release_carried`, `clear_carry_ref`, `sync_section` (MSA-26, MSA-27). `condition_bp` carries through, so installing a FAILED-hp instance installs a FAILED module (IDB-17, IDB-18). There is **no `remove_module`** in the MVP: V8 salvage is the only way a module leaves INSTALLED, so the choice at the hardpoint is final (MSA-28). The Item DB's `T_cycle` — **cut + carry + `cap_port` on the stubs + install** (Interaction's and Assembly's verbs) — is the cost of one salvage-then-reinstall (IDB F-15); repeated as Assembly asks (MSA T12): the install precondition is *carried, compatible per `compatible_defs(h)`, at a hardpoint*. The patch cap and decay clock persist through salvage and reinstall (IDB-18, provisional on a Graph ruling, IDB OQ-10). The welder and section cut cannot run while carrying (MSA-26). *Why.* The install is the one place where the haul becomes the ship, and a seat with no take-back is what makes the take at the derelict a commitment; repeating the precondition keeps the sortie's last step from being read as inventory management. *Pillar.* P5; anti-pillar (not a freeform builder). *Decided.* run ruling R3.

**BS-19 — A dark dock must never be fatal: the hop-availability invariant (ruled 2026-10-27: the pod's status glow).** *Rule.* **No sortie state exists in which the hop is unavailable for want of light alone.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Mechanism (user ruling, OQ-BS-4 part (a), X2, D58, D70a):** the docked pod's dock-room prop carries a small **self-powered status glow** that counts as an **ordinary lit fixture** and not as a fourth `act_gate` exception: the POD_CONSOLE stands inside the glow's light shape, so `lit(POD_CONSOLE)` holds at every docked pod whatever the beam cell or the stick count, and `pod_hop` cannot answer `NOT_LIT` while the glow stands. The glow guarantees `lit(POD_CONSOLE)` at every docked pod; the DOCK_CONSOLE at the home airlock keeps its own lit gate and is not part of this invariant (IA-6, IA-40) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Interaction's refusal of a `pod_hop` lit exemption (IA-6, Open Question 31) **stands**; BS-5's lit-only rule has no exemption for the console. The glow belongs to the pod and not to the derelict bus, so it needs neither the player's cell nor a lit pickup nor a woken bus. **Ownership is joint:** Emitter State and Web Map guarantee the glow (LANDED: Emitter EM-3 (self-powered fixture class, subkind DOCK_STATUS) and EM-11, mutator E10 `set_dock_status` (called by Web Map in the `pod_at` apply) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; Web Map reverses its ASK-BS-W2 answer and accepts ASK-BS-W3), Derelict Authoring places it in every dock room and lints the placement, including that the console lies inside the glow's light shape, as a build error, and the art-director separates its luminance from the visible-unknown lamp (DA-27) and keeps it steady and un-modulated; Boarding states the invariant and its acceptance (AC-BS-51b, AC-BS-92). The glow is ON while the pod is docked and SYSTEM-switched (the player cannot switch it; Emitter State EM-3/EM-11), with its light footprint limited to the console cell *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, so it is an `I_light` term of every aboard row of D.2 (its output is `DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` 500, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX` 48 [PLACEHOLDER: Emitter], section emission at most 24 (Emitter C3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; Attention must count it in its unswitchable set and recheck the abort floor, a note for Attention).

*Cell policy (OQ-BS-4 part (b), X5, D70b, user ruling):* V7 `top_up` joins the MVP verb list (the Graph's LS-26 amendment) as a deliberate bare-hand TAP; `TOPUP_MODE` is VERB and `CELL_ENABLED` is on, so the lamp cell exists, is finite, and is refillable at a lit BATTERY port at home (Suit D.9: a credit never exceeds the deficit), and the Pillar 3 'go dark' lever exists. A spent cell therefore costs the sortie its light and not the way home. *What remains true.* A module dropped far from the dock in the dark still needs light to be re-taken (`pickup` is lit-only, BS-5; EC-BS-30), so with the cell spent and no sticks it is lost to that sortie: a cost and not a soft-lock, because the player walks to the lit console and hops. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

*History, kept so the acceptance rows read.* Before the ruling, a player with the cell spent, zero sticks and an unlit console was in a true soft-lock and it was the expected end of a long lit session (D.10: about 4 survey sorties spend the cell), with the dock survivable (`a_dock` `T0` -6000 mC) so that no death and no restore ever fired; Interaction had refused the lit exemption, Web Map had declined the stronger lint, and the loose-glowstick fallback was unsound (a loose stick is unlit until thrown and `pickup` is lit-only). The existing mitigations (the two-stick `a_dock` shelf, `ls_a_dock_shelf`; the four-stick home airlock supply, `ls_air_locker`, DA-26; drop, throw, re-take, IA-29) still narrow the dark-drop case and are no longer load-bearing for the hop. **The invariant is BLOCKING for the implementation of this system** (stage-12 ruling after the CD-GDD-ALIGN concern: P5 says failure costs ship and body and never a soft-lock): the sortie is not implementation-complete, and the slice does not ship, while AC-BS-92 (a bounded reachability test over the matrix and the campaign-length strand cell) or AC-BS-51b (the placement lint and the console-in-glow check) is red; no sign-off replaces them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

*Mechanisms considered (history of the ruling).* **M1**, a console-only lit exemption in IA-6, was refused by Interaction and is not taken. **M3**, a reserved lamp charge only the console press can spend, was not taken. **M2**, a pod-owned console lamp, is the nearest: the ruled mechanism is a self-powered status glow on the docked pod's prop, an ordinary fixture and not a lamp off the derelict bus. Rejected throughout: allowing `throw_glowstick` while carrying (it removes the BS-5 cost of lighting the drop zone first). *Pillar.* P5, P2. *Decided.* run ruling R3 (level-designer LD-R6); the stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN revision made the invariant binding; the user ruled the mechanism and the cell policy on 2026-10-27 (OQ-BS-4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**BS-20 — Content-side sortie constraints are citations; one design target.** *Rule.* These Derelict Authoring bounds are lint-backed facts Boarding relies on and re-checks across **all five loaded sets** S0 to S4 and both sortie orders (never only the first sortie): a carried round trip to the farthest salvage through an unbreathable stretch inside Suit's vacuum budget `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s (22 tiles each way walking out and carrying back, 34 carried both ways; AC-SE-75a); A has no unbreathable stretch, so it binds B only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*; a hazard crossing of at most 7 tiles of lethal cold (5.6 s); `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 1800, 600 when carrying (the endogenous-fault escape bound, DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound); 18 / 22 module nodes (A / B); four loose parts *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the loose ledger (DA-28, DA-29, DA-21, DA-25, DA-26, DA-32). **Design target, not a lint and not registered:** a first sortie to A completes cut and carry-home in about five minutes of *player time* (concept Core Loop; measured as W_LOOP, home console press to install, with its median W_ABOARD part kept below Sanity's stage-1 point, D.1 and D.8; a long sortie that enters stage 1 is intended: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D73 part (c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* with `RESERVE_S` [PLACEHOLDER] and `CELL_S` [PLACEHOLDER] sufficient. The route itself is a minute-scale lower bound; the five minutes are listening, lighting, deciding and door choices, so nobody tunes the route up to hit five minutes by distance (`V_CARRY` is locked). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **One target:** W_LOOP (home console press to install) is the single five-minute target and every other figure derives from it: the design-expectation W_ABOARD is W_LOOP less the non-interactive pod legs and the home leg, about 259 s at the defaults, of which the lint guarantees about 229 s (Tuning Knobs, Design targets; OQ-BS-28 (d)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and the 300 s figure of D.8 and the 5-minute top of the X-BS-1 band are the stage-1 ceiling on the median, not second targets. The ruled decision carry of about 21 to 28 tiles (X3) lies with at most 7 tiles (336 px) of it inside `a_machine` (the lethal-cold cap, DA-28; DA-48 measures the carry from the cut point and its proposal puts 228 px there) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; whether a 1008 to 1344 px carried leg passes `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 600 when carrying (DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound) is Derelict Authoring's lint question (OQ-BS-31). This GDD's reading: the 600 px bound is the endogenous-fault escape bound and does not apply to a non-fault decision carry; Derelict Authoring states that it does not (DA-29, DA-48, AC-DA-161): no exemption is granted or needed, and a lint that rejects the ruled route fails AC-BS-52 (ASK-BS-D4 (e)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Sanity's dwell cost is cited and not set: `ABOARD_EXPOSURE` [PLACEHOLDER] (SN). **Subject budget:** Boarding adds no subject beyond the drops `P <= PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` and forbids any rule here that seeds more loose items; the post-weld sortie S4 `{home+B, A}` already exceeds `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` by 24 (144 vs 120, DA OQ-DA-20, owned by Derelict Authoring and Interaction, C-BS-7). Node anchors are not published by Derelict Authoring, so every route figure in this GDD is marked as assumed and deferred to Layout's `route_length_px` (ASK-BS-D1). *Why.* The authored bounds are what keep a carried return survivable and a retreat legal across every loaded set; citing them and minting no lint of Boarding's own keeps Derelict Authoring the one owner of the geometry, while the design target names only the felt length. *Pillar.* P2, P5. *Decided.* run rulings R23, R24, R29.

**BS-21 — Autosave after a cut.** *Rule.* "Section extraction" in SL-4 is **Assembly's detach** (BDY:341) and is already served by MSA-33's derived read `last_shape_change_T()`, polled by Save/Load; Boarding neither owns nor names it. For a **module** cut, a completed V8 should also shorten the loss window, following the same pattern: Interaction publishes a pure derived read of the last salvage-completion tick (the read `last_salvage_T()` (registry: `last_salvage_T`); **Boarding mints no name**, which is this GDD's answer to Save/Load OQ-24), Save/Load polls it under SL-5's gate and `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, and `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` guards a doomed save (SL-4, SL-5, SL-7, SL-8). A tell defers through SL-5 soft row (b) (provisional; an absent Attention view counts as open and logs `GATE_INPUT_ABSENT`); a channel, stagger or transit defers through `GATE_SOFT_STATES`; DOWNED and DEAD are hard. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **User rulings X7, D14, D42, D17:** (a) any bound seat whose `vitals_state` is CRITICAL or worse is a third soft-gate input (a due save is deferred up to the cap, then written `RISKY`, with no glyph), also applied to `quit_risky`; (b) the fairness step-back: a death restore also steps back one generation when `T_downed - g_r.T` is under `W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE` (600 ticks); (c) a post-DOWNED refractory of `W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE` ticks. The module-cut event autosave, with the weld and seam-cut events, is **confirmed** (D17; the escape hatch is a data change and metric M5). Assembly's seam-cut event autosave is withheld while the self-inflicted RAGGED decompression runs (until the keep-side cut room has vented and its ports are capped or past the port ceiling, D54, MSA-33) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and does not apply to a module cut, whose SEVERED descriptors are EXOGENOUS and open no row (a) window; the fault loss window (mean about 5400, max 10,800, ceiling 18,000 ticks, D55) is Assembly's and Save/Load's. The ruled text is Save/Load's (SL-5, SL-8); D.9 prints the gate list. `CARRY_WALK` is not a gate state, so an autosave may land mid-carry; a cut's SEVERED descriptors are EXOGENOUS and open no row (a) window. The read therefore cannot trap the player in a doomed state. The brief's push-event idea is not adopted (Boarding cannot emit one, BS-1). *Why.* The loss ceiling (340 s, 5.7 minutes: SL's `loss_max` of 20,400 ticks, D.9) is longer than a whole five-minute sortie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Pillar.* P5 (loss is not total). *Decided.* run ruling R6; ASK-BS-I4, ASK-BS-L1.

**BS-22 — Art direction owned here: severed stubs, the cap piece, and one shared carried-module sprite.** *Rule.* Boarding owns the **art direction and states** of the severed-stub pieces (kit gap K-9; DA:526, DA:1341, DA:1465) for `/asset-spec`: one STUB per open fluid port; hissing until capped (the sound is Audio's); a cap piece after `begin_cap`; the pedestal rect stays (LY-20) and the scorched kerf is Interaction's V8 completion row; all **hue-less, matte, mechanical, no glow, no body vocabulary in any sprite, palette or sound brief** (ART 4.4; the flesh and violet palette is reserved for sanity leaks). All carried modules, real or (VS-A) phantom, draw as **one plain shape drawn once on the tool layer** (ART:512, ART:815), so a real and a phantom carry look alike; identity is known from the loose sprite at pickup and from the body cue, not from the carried sprite (closes IA Open Question 23). The carry frames keep the chest point and the forward beam arc unobstructed (ART:1221); pose is **ruled by the art-director: the module is held overhead**, centred over the helmet with its bottom edge at least 2 px above the crown, the sprite capped at 24 x 14 px so figure plus module is at most 71 px, under the 72 px wall front face (ART 8.2; AD-BS-1, AD-BS-2; C-BS-5 closed). The PC-8 phrase "below the lamp" is refreshed (refresh row 19). *Why.* A hue-less, matte stub stays on the truth side of the sane palette, and one shared carried sprite means a real and a phantom carry can be told apart only by the body cue and the checks, never by the drawing. *Pillar.* P1, P4 (parity). *Decided.* run rulings R21, R22.

**BS-23 — Loose items and the sortie: what Boarding repeats.** *Rule.* Placement data is Derelict Authoring's ledger (DA-26), slots are Layout's (LY-22), the mechanism and holder are Interaction's (IA-28); Boarding adds only the sortie-level rules stated in BS-13 (abandon persists), BS-5 (dark drop needs light), BS-16 (the haul is finite). A module dropped then left on a section that is later welded or cut off moves with the section (items are section-local, LY-22). Wording refreshes owed to neighbours that say otherwise are listed in Cross-References and never edited here. *Why.* Restating loose-item ownership here would give one fact two writers; naming only the sortie-level consequences (abandon persists, a dark drop needs light, the haul is finite) keeps one owner per fact. *Pillar.* P5. *Decided.* run ruling R20.

**BS-24 — What Boarding refuses (the anti-pillar rule).** *Rule.* The following do not exist in the sortie, and a rule anywhere in this GDD that implies one is a defect:

| Refusal | Guard | Pillar or anti-pillar |
|---|---|---|
| Combat: no weapon on any def, no damage verb, no kill; the cutter cuts machines, never creatures | G-1 | not a combat game |
| Progression: nothing levels, unlocks or scores from salvage; the only progression is the ship's body and what the player learns (the knowledge persistence the failure contract depends on is not a progression this guard forbids) | G-2 | P5 / not a combat game |
| Construction: modules are pre-shaped; a take is an extraction and not a relocation; no `remove_module` | G-3 | not a freeform builder |
| Economy: no shop, currency, recipe, vendor, refill, loot table, rarity; salvage-once | G-4 | P5 |
| Readouts: no inventory screen, pack capacity, encumbrance meter, weight, value, condition or capacity number, pod scale | G-5 | P1 |
| Timers and meters: no sortie timer, no Attention meter (visual or audio), no `listen` verb | G-6 | P3 |
| Forced script: sortie order is a recommendation (DA-2); no forced drop, cap, required module or quest item; no payoff-less carry taught as the reference cut | G-7 | no authored story; P1 |
| PvP: no stealing from a crewmate's hands and no reward for harm (VS-B); the carry cost is the crew's shared cost; the only harm to a crewmate is the system-gated friendly-harm act, admitted only while the attacker's sanity is system-verified below the harm threshold (Sanity; IA-31), with a victim-visible tell and attribution to the web, so a sane player has no attack (P4(c)) | G-8 | no intentional PvP; P4(c) |
| Body metaphor in the senses: graft, severed, bleed are design prose only | G-9 | P1 sane palette |
| A win state in a haul: no "complete the ship", no collection checklist | G-10 | no win state |
| A price that lies (BS-15) | G-11 | P4 |

Restraint and retreat are legal strategies with stated costs (BS-13). *Pillar.* the anti-pillars. *Decided.* run ruling R31; creative-director guard rails G-1 to G-11.

# TRs: Boarding & Salvage (boarding)

Source: design/gdd/boarding-and-salvage.md (composition system, zero runtime footprint).

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-boarding-001 | The system registers no state block, step hook, command type, mutator, read view, notification, registry constant or Debug Overlay diagnostics channel; no scene-tree code of its own (verifiable: registry delta is only referenced_by entries). | Core | BS-1 |
| TR-boarding-002 | Sortie step order (prepare, board, enter, listen, light, decide, position, cut, cap-or-leave, pick up, carry, hop, install, settle) is composed from existing owners and stores no sortie state; it reuses `loco_state`, Attention `phase` and `transit_state` by reference. | Core | BS-2 |
| TR-boarding-003 | While carrying, exactly four interactions are admitted: `drop`, `install_module` on a compatible HARDPOINT, `pod_hop` on POD_CONSOLE, and V4 `set_opening` on a door face; all other targets stay prompt-less and `BUSY`. | Input | BS-9, BS-10 |
| TR-boarding-004 | A cut yield is never auto-carried; pickup is a lit TAP moving LOOSE_WORLD to CARRIED via `set_carry_ref` (Controller) and `set_carried` (Suit), one carried instance per seat. | Core | BS-9 |
| TR-boarding-005 | `carry_ref` and the Suit carried instance are restored together and cross-checked on load (mismatch raises `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`); Interaction `post_restore` never touches `carry_ref`; in-progress channels are dropped with a RESTORE abort. | Save/Load | EC-BS-39 (Edge G) |
| TR-boarding-006 | A cut is lit-only: every channelled/object-addressed sortie verb obeys `act_gate(o) = in_reach(o) AND lit(o)`; no dark exemption exists for extraction or the console. | Core | BS-5 |
| TR-boarding-007 | Carry speed is `V_CARRY` (no run) independent of module mass; mass never alters `V_CARRY` or carry noise, and no weight number, pack capacity or encumbrance meter exists (weight only via Suit `cue_load`). | Core | BS-11 |
| TR-boarding-008 | A stowed HEAVY item disables run (Controller rule PC-8); roster owned by Item DB. | Core | BS-11 (D18) |
| TR-boarding-009 | The pod hop carries per seat one `carry_ref` plus STOWED stacks; capacity is seat count (one at MVP); one module per hop; `carry_ref` is intact on arrival; no refusal reason may read module-body state. | Core | BS-12 |
| TR-boarding-010 | `pod_hop` must always be allowed during TELL/BREACH (escape verb); departure from non-home locus ends a BREACH and voids due-run breach when all recorded seats have left. | Core | BS-13 (a)(b), WM-26, AT-22 |
| TR-boarding-011 | `drop` of the carried module is legal anywhere, free, exempt from the lit rule; downed actor drops the module within one tick (Controller clears `carry_ref`, Interaction hook at divisor 1 runs after). | Core | BS-13 (d)(e) |
| TR-boarding-012 | Abandoned modules persist in `loose[]` and a left derelict persists exactly as left (dormant, state stands still); salvage is salvage-once and a SALVAGED slot is a permanent tombstone. | Save/Load | BS-13, BS-16 |
| TR-boarding-013 | Hop-availability invariant: no sortie state exists where `pod_hop` is unavailable for want of light alone; docked pod carries a self-powered status glow (Emitter subkind DOCK_STATUS, set via `set_dock_status` E10) that lights POD_CONSOLE; BLOCKING until AC-BS-92 and AC-BS-51b pass. | Rendering | BS-19 |
| TR-boarding-014 | Derelict dock rooms must have the status glow placed and linted so the POD_CONSOLE lies inside the glow light shape (build error otherwise). | Data | BS-19 |
| TR-boarding-015 | Carry burden `U_BURDEN` Attention intake is pushed per tick only while salvage is held aboard the non-home locus body where it was taken (not IN_POD/DOWNED/DEAD), moving or not; it stops in the pod and does not resume at home. | Threading/Timing | BS-12, Dependencies row 6/8, EC-BS-63 |
| TR-boarding-016 | A completed module cut (V8 `salvage_node`) must be observable by Save/Load via Interaction's pure derived read `last_salvage_T()` polled under the SL-5 gate and `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`; Boarding mints no name or event. | Save/Load | BS-21 |
| TR-boarding-017 | Autosave is legal mid-carry (CARRY_WALK is not a gate state); channel, stagger and transit defer via `GATE_SOFT_STATES`; DOWNED/DEAD are hard gates; a tell defers via SL-5 soft row (b); CRITICAL vitals is a third soft input. | Save/Load | BS-21, EC-BS-40/41 (Edge G) |
| TR-boarding-018 | Threat draws (tell length) are re-keyed per restore epoch (death restore advances; newest Save & Quit Continue keeps; stored in per-slot `slot_epoch.bin`) while Graph physical failures and persisted counters replay exactly (determinism). | Save/Load | EC-BS-42 (Edge G), X8 |
| TR-boarding-019 | Yield is deterministic (`salvage_yield`, no RNG) and `condition_bp` carries through install, so installing a FAILED-hp instance installs a FAILED module; no `remove_module` exists. | Data | BS-16, BS-18 |
| TR-boarding-020 | `install_module` prompt exists iff the carried def is in `compatible_defs(h)` of the focused HARDPOINT; chain M5 `install_module`, `release_carried`, `clear_carry_ref`, `sync_section`. | Core | BS-18 |
| TR-boarding-021 | Cut completion registers one STUB per `open_end` fluid port; uncapped stubs hiss indefinitely with no forcing timer; `begin_cap` is hands-free-only (welder) and ledger-resumable; power-only modules leave no stub. | Core | BS-7, BS-8 |
| TR-boarding-022 | Cut is a CHANNEL of `SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS` whose effect lands at completion only; abort leaves module in place and keeps the partial ledger for `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`; second seat on same node is `BUSY`. | Threading/Timing | BS-7 |
| TR-boarding-023 | Price channels (noise, hiss, load breath, pace, time, air) are never altered by hallucination; only the prize may lie (class (b) lies only at MVP; class (d) deferred). | Core | BS-15 |
| TR-boarding-024 | No readouts of value/condition/Attention exist: no value tag, rating, condition bar, inventory screen, sortie timer, `listen` verb, or Attention meter (visual or audio). | UI | BS-6, BS-24 (G-5, G-6) |
| TR-boarding-025 | Content must satisfy Derelict Authoring lints across all five loaded sets S0-S4 and both sortie orders: carried round trip within `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s, hazard crossing at most 7 tiles lethal cold, `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 1800 (600 carrying), 18/22 module nodes A/B, loose ledger of 9 placements. | Data | BS-20 |
| TR-boarding-026 | Carried modules render as one shared plain shape on the tool layer (max 24x14 px, held overhead, figure plus module at most 71 px); stub/cap/kerf art is hue-less and matte (no flesh/violet palette). | Rendering | BS-22 |
| TR-boarding-027 | All Boarding values are integer tick/AU arithmetic over owners' registered constants (TICK_RATE, V_CARRY, TILE_PX etc.); no wall-clock performance criterion of its own; frame-time pending spike on RM-DESKTOP (P99 16.6 ms) / RM-DECK (P99 33.3 ms). | Performance | Header X14/R12, BS-1 |
| TR-boarding-028 | No combat, progression, economy, construction freedom, forced-script drop/cap, or win-state is implemented (hard never-do list G-1..G-11). | Core | BS-24 |
| TR-boarding-029 | Berth is LOUD (one `U_LOUD` push at apply) and unberth QUIET; berth/unberth sit on DOCK_CONSOLE and are BUSY while carrying. | Core | BS-9 (D59) |

## Public surface

Owns no APIs, state, commands, signals or registry constants (BS-1). It owns only design-time rules:
- Sortie sequence (14 steps, BS-2); carry-admitted set (BS-9, four verbs); pod-hop cargo rule (BS-12); field-check procedure and ladder (BS-14); retreat/abandon conditions a-e (BS-13); stub-capping policy (BS-8); hop-availability invariant (BS-19); severed-stub / cap / carried-module art direction (BS-22); design-time formulas D.1 `route_ticks` to D.10 `lamp_cell_budget` (including `tell_window_fit`, `sortie_noise_budget`, `hazard_dwell_budget`, `cap_versus_leave`, `modules_per_fuel`, `check_cost_ratio`, `sortie_dwell_envelope`, `loss_window_after_cut`).
- Does NOT own: `loose[]`/`stubs[]` (Interaction IA-28), `carried` (Suit SE-13), `carry_ref` (Controller PC-8), `pod_at` (Web Map).

## Consumes

- Interaction: `pickup`, `drop`, `begin_cut` (V8 / M6 `salvage_node`), `begin_cap` (M12 `cap_port`), `field_check`, `throw_glowstick`, `place_loose`, `loose[]`, `stubs[]`, `act_gate`, abort set, `push_stimulus`, V4 `set_opening` (`admitted_while_carrying`), POD_CONSOLE `pod_hop`/HARDPOINT `install_module` rows, derived read `last_salvage_T()`.
- Suit & Equipment: carried instance (`set_carried`), stowed stacks, tool slots, `equip_tool`, `cue_load`, `RESERVE_S`, `CELL_S`, glowsticks, `VACUUM_BUDGET_S`.
- Modular Ship Assembly: `install_module`, `release_carried`, `clear_carry_ref`, `sync_section`, `compatible_defs(h)`, `last_shape_change_T()`, carve-out C1.
- Derelict Authoring: `loose_slots`, module placements (`def_id`, `hp`), `entry_room_key`, loose ledger, dried trails, hazard-room bounds, five loaded sets, lints.
- Item & Module Database: `salvage_yield`, `carry_class`, `mass_g`, stub leak rates, `T_cycle`.
- Player Controller: `carry_ref`, `set_carry_ref`, gait/`V_CARRY`, `NOISE_PER_TICK`, per-tick `burden_T` push (PC-10, D.13).
- Life-Support Graph: M6, M12, `open_end`, consequence channel (LSG:44), LS-13/LS-17.
- Attention: `push_stimulus` units, `U_BURDEN` (`carry_burden_intake`), tell window, abort, `attention_arm_tell`.
- Web Map & Transit: `pod_hop`, POD_CONSOLE, arrival envelope, fuel/leg constants, dormancy, `set_dock_status` caller.
- Emitter State: DOCK_STATUS fixture (EM-3, EM-11, E10); exposure table for lit jobs.
- Save/Load: SL-4, SL-5 gate, `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, `GATE_SOFT_STATES`, `slot_epoch.bin`.
- Sanity: `record_falsification`, SN-21 ladder, `ABOARD_EXPOSURE`.
- Layout (`room_at`, `route_length_px`), Body Physics (`actor_section`), Failure & Trail (dried-trail field check), Horror (places nothing), Perception Filter / Adaptive Audio (class (d) tell, event list), HUD, In-World Instruments, Command & Simulation Layer (registration contract, unused).

## Engine risk

GDD states no scripting/gameplay-logic engine file applies; pure rule composition and integer arithmetic.
- Typed-return overrides for handler base classes (4.7), relevant to Interaction/Assembly handlers, not Boarding: HIGH.
- Light/exposure (lit-object queries, self-powered DOCK_STATUS light fixture, 2D lighting and occlusion): LOW to MEDIUM for Light2D (older API; 4.5-4.7 lighting changes unspecified in the GDD).
- Release export on Godot 4.7.2 `forward_plus` for the reference machines: HIGH (version-pinned measurement target).
- AudioServer for the audio event list (hiss, creak, tell bed): LOW.
- Overall Boarding engine risk: LOW (HIGH only via the 4.7 typed-return note in neighbours).
